We got template 29646 retro_smarts: '[C:2]-[OH;D1;+0:1]>>C-C(-C)(-C)-[Si](-C)(-C)-[O;H0;D2;+0:1]-[C:2]'

So retrosynthetic direction: alcohol (C-OH) to a silyl ether with tert-butyl groups? Actually forward: C-C(-C)(-C)-[Si](-C)(-C)-[O]... -> alcohol. So retro: break C-O bond to give silyl protected alcohol? Wait retro_smarts shows reactants: [C:2]-[OH] (alcohol) -> product: C-C(-C)(-C)-[Si](-C)(-C)-[O]-[C:2] (silyl ether). So applying retro to target will replace an OH with a silyl ether group. Our target has multiple OH groups: one primary alcohol at side chain? Actually target: O[C@H]1C[C@@H](O[C@@H]([C@@H]1C)/C=C(CO)/C)C/C=C/C=C/C(O)=O. Contains a phenolic? Not phenol. There's a primary alcohol (CO) attached to double bond side chain? There's also a carboxylic acid (C(O)=O). Also an ether linking to sugar-like ring.

Template 29646 likely used to protect an alcohol as a silyl ether. So first step could be protecting a primary alcohol (maybe the CO side chain) with a silyl group.

But we need to produce a route; we can propose plausible steps even if not chemically perfect, as long as templates match. We need to verify each step using verify_step maybe. Let's attempt to apply template 29646 to target to see possible precursors. Use apply_template.
